title: Sultan Baybars and the Sixteen Captains of Police

full_text:
Sultan Al-Malik al-Zahir Rukn al-Din Baybars sat upon his throne in the Citadel of Cairo, surrounded by his ministers and the Sixteen Captains of Police who governed the sixteen quarters of the metropolis.

Desiring to test their detective acumen and integrity, the Sultan commanded:

'Let each of the sixteen captains recount the most extraordinary case of detection he has ever resolved in his quarter, that I may see who among you truly understands how to protect the innocent and uncover the truth without relying upon the rod of torture!'

The audience hall fell silent, and the Sixteen Captains stepped forward in turn to present their chronicles of criminal detection, intricate judicial inquiries, and the triumph of observant justice over cunning deceits across the alleys of Cairo.
moral: Keen detective observation, empathy, and justice protect the peace of a great metropolis.
